target.title: fix(lmstudio): set supportsTools only for native tool-trained models
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LM Studio discovery already reads `capabilities.trained_for_tool_use`, but catalog `compat` never set `supportsTools`. Native-trained models therefore relied only on core’s permissive default, with no explicit catalog signal when LM Studio reports native tool training.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper re-review (and LM Studio’s documented tools contract) showed that `trained_for_tool_use: false` means “untrained / less reliable default tool mode”, not “tools unsupported”. Mapping false → `compat.supportsTools: false` would silently strip tools from existing users.

This revision only maps `trained_for_tool_use: true` → `compat.supportsTools: true`. False and omitted stay unset so OpenClaw keeps the permissive default (`supportsTools !== false`) and LM Studio’s default tool-use path remains available. Native quality still surfaces via the existing `trainedForToolUse` / `tool-use` tag path.

AI-assisted: yes. I inspected the LM Studio wire mapper, discovery spread into catalog compat, sibling Venice/Ollama `supportsTools` semantics, and LM Studio’s OpenAI-compat tools docs before the change.

## User Impact

Models LM Studio marks as natively trained for tools get an explicit `supportsTools: true` catalog flag. Models that report `false` or omit the field keep tools enabled (no capability regression on upgrade).

## Evidence

**Real-machine production-path proof (L3):** macOS `darwin 21.6.0 x64`, Node `v22.19.0`. No desktop LM Studio process was listening on `:1234`, so the harness started a real localhost HTTP server that speaks LM Studio’s `/api/v1/models` wire shape (including `trained_for_tool_use`), then called production `discoverLmstudioModels` + runtime `supportsModelTools` with no mocked mapper/discovery.

**Before (current main catalog shape):** native-trained models keep only streaming compat — no `supportsTools`:

```json
{
  "id": "demo-native-tools",
  "name": "demo-native-tools (tool-use)",
  "compat": { "supportsUsageInStreaming": true },
  "toolsAllowedByRuntime": true
}
```

**After (PR tip `5e1d39e7089ba02fa13c29a280560b6eac26dcfb`):** the same live discovery adds explicit tools metadata only for native-trained models; untrained/unknown stay unset and still allow tools:

```json
{
  "native": {
    "id": "demo-native-tools",
    "compat": { "supportsTools": true, "supportsUsageInStreaming": true },
    "toolsAllowedByRuntime": true
  },
  "untrained": {
    "id": "demo-untrained-tools",
    "compat": { "supportsUsageInStreaming": true },
    "toolsAllowedByRuntime": true
  },
  "unknown": {
    "id": "demo-unknown-tools",
    "compat": { "supportsUsageInStreaming": true },
    "toolsAllowedByRuntime": true
  }
}
```

Observable after-fix diff vs main: catalog consumers that read `compat.supportsTools` now see `true` for native-trained LM Studio models; runtime tool gating (`supportsModelTools`) remains permissive for false/omitted (no upgrade regression).

| Layer | Proof | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | `mapLmstudioWireEntry`: true → `supportsTools: true`; false/omitted → unset | pass |
| L2 | `discoverLmstudioModels` spreads `base.compat` into catalog entries | pass |
| L3 | Live HTTP `/api/v1/models` → production discovery → catalog + `supportsModelTools` before/after above | pass |
| Gate | `oxfmt` + `oxlint` + focused vitest | pass |

```text
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/lmstudio/src/models.test.ts -t "trained_for_tool_use|maps trained"
→ 1 passed (26 skipped)
```

Head: `5e1d39e7089ba02fa13c29a280560b6eac26dcfb`

```text
extensions/lmstudio/src/models.ts       +28 -1
extensions/lmstudio/src/models.test.ts  +29 -0
```
